question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution outlines the principle of just and humane conditions of work?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 42**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 42** of the Indian Constitution directs the State to ensure the provision of just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief.
 
• This article is part of the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**, which are non-justiciable but serve as guiding principles for governance.
 
• It emphasizes the responsibility of the State to improve labor conditions and promote social justice.
 
• The provision aims to protect workers' rights and promote welfare measures, particularly for women workers and marginalized laborers.
 
• It serves as a basis for labor laws and welfare schemes aimed at improving workplace conditions and maternity benefits in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP):**

 
 
• Part IV (Articles 36–51) of the Indian Constitution contains the DPSPs, which are guidelines for the State to ensure socio-economic justice.
 
• They are not enforceable by courts but are fundamental in policymaking and governance.
 
 
 
• **Labor Welfare in India:**
 
 
• India has implemented various labor laws, such as the Factories Act, 1948, and the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, to ensure humane working conditions and maternity relief.
 
• These laws are influenced by the principles enshrined in Article 42.
 
 
 
• **Social Justice:**
 
 
• Article 42 promotes social justice by advocating for equitable working conditions and support for vulnerable workers.
 
• It aligns with global labor standards set by institutions like the International Labour Organization (ILO).
 
 
 
• **Maternity Relief:**
 
 
• Article 42 specifically mentions maternity relief, emphasizing the need for paid leave and health benefits for women workers.
 
• The Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017, which provides 26 weeks of paid maternity leave, is a significant step in this direction.
